docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The Mṛcchakaṭika, the most realistic of Sanskrit plays: in the city of Ujjayinī the impoverished merchant-Brahman Cārudatta and the courtesan Vasantasenā fall in love, the king’s brother-in-law plots against them, and a political revolution brings the ten acts to their end. Translated from the Sanskrit and Prakrit by Arthur W. Ryder (1877–1938) as volume 9 of the Harvard Oriental Series (1905).

From Wikisource · Public domain

The Little Clay Cart, translated by Arthur W. Ryder (1877–1938), Harvard Oriental Series 9, 1905, as proofread on English Wikisource by its contributors. This book is not stored in this library: each chapter is read from Wikisource when it is opened, shown in this library's format, and ends with its own attribution. Licence: Public domain.
